# TAO (JUNO-TAO), arXiv:2610.23331v1, Fig. 26: SMOOTHED energy leakage + non-linearity response matrix
# P(E_vis bin | E_true) for the fiducial volume R <= 800 mm, built from the pixel extraction in
# TAO_Fig26_leakage_matrix.txt. E_true = T_e+ + 1.022 MeV; E_vis = visible energy with non-linearity, before
# energy-resolution smearing.
#
# Method:
#  1. Peak position: the full-containment band follows E_vis = E_true * f_e+(E_true), with f_e+ the nominal TAO
#     positron non-linearity (Fig. 25b, TAO_Fig25b_nonlinearity.txt). The extracted matrix confirms this to
#     within a pixel (0.012 MeV) at all energies.
#  2. Shape: the distribution of delta = E_vis - E_peak was found to be nearly independent of E_true: a sharp
#     full-containment peak (~60% within +-0.05 MeV), a shoulder from partial Compton escape, a bump near
#     delta = -0.45 MeV (one 511-keV gamma escaping) and a far tail that grows slowly with energy (positron
#     kinetic-energy leakage). Six templates in delta (0.01-MeV bins) were built by stacking the pixel columns,
#     weighted by counts, in the E_true bands 1.02-1.5, 1.5-2.5, 2.5-3.5, 3.5-4.5, 4.5-6.0 and 6.0-11.5 MeV
#     (count-weighted centres 1.34, 2.08, 3.00, 3.96, 5.08, 6.72 MeV). The tail (delta < -0.03 MeV) was smoothed with
#     a Gaussian of 0.02 MeV; the peak is kept as stacked.
#  3. Each E_true column uses the template linearly interpolated in E_true between band centres (held constant
#     below 1.34 and above 6.72 MeV), shifted to E_peak(E_true) and integrated over each E_vis bin.
#  Count-weighted stacking is needed because the figure samples only one 5-keV bin per pixel; per-column
#  normalisation would be biased whenever a column's sampled rows miss the narrow peak.
#
# Grid: matches the forward model in Newtrinos (juno_rewrite.jl): E_true bins 0.70-12.00 MeV and E_vis bins
# 0.70-13.00 MeV, both 0.02 MeV wide. E_vis extends to 13 MeV because the non-linearity pushes E_vis above E_true
# at high energy. Columns with E_true < 1.022 MeV are empty.
# Column sums are the probability that E_vis >= 0.70 MeV: below 1 near threshold (0.80 at E_true = 1.03 MeV,
# 0.91 at 1.25 MeV, > 0.997 above 1.5 MeV), i.e. events falling below the 0.7-MeV selection are lost, not
# renormalised.
#
# Validation against the raw extraction (fractions in delta windows, count-weighted, +-0.25 MeV in E_true):
#  agrees to 0.01-0.03 in absolute fraction from 2 to 7 MeV; differences of this size come mostly from the
#  0.02-MeV E_vis binning across the steep shoulder just below the peak. Above ~8 MeV the raw matrix has too few
#  events to test; the 6.0-11.5 MeV template (dominated by 6-7 MeV) is used there.
# Limitations: the peak position is tied to the NOMINAL TAO non-linearity; to propagate non-linearity
# uncertainties, shift E_peak by the e+ band rather than using this matrix as fixed. The simulation statistics
# behind Fig. 26 limit the precision of the far tail (delta < -1 MeV, ~1-2% of events) to roughly 20-30%.
#
# Format: sparse list of non-zero entries (P > 1e-8).
#  E_true_lo  E_true_hi  E_vis_lo  E_vis_hi  P   (P = probability for the E_vis bin, given E_true at the bin centre)
#
#E_true_lo E_true_hi E_vis_lo E_vis_hi P
